title: NEURONOPATHY, DISTAL HEREDITARY MOTOR, AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT 11

relationships.phenotype: NEURONOPATHY, DISTAL HEREDITARY MOTOR, AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT 11

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that autosomal dominant distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-11 (HMND11) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the SPTAN1 gene (182810) on chromosome 9q34.

checks.claim: Autosomal dominant distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-11 (HMND11) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the SPTAN1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified patients with heterozygous nonsense mutations in the αII-spectrin gene, SPTAN1, in three separate dominant hereditary motor neuropathy families via next-generation sequencing.
checks.explanation: The paper reports heterozygous SPTAN1 mutations in dominant distal HMN families. The HMND11 name is OMIM's own label.

checks.claim: The SPTAN1 gene is located on chromosome 9q34.
checks.evidence_quote: heterozygous nonsense mutations in the αII-spectrin gene, SPTAN1
checks.explanation: The chromosome location is standard nomenclature and isn't stated in the abstract.

paragraphs.text: Autosomal dominant distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-11 (HMND11) is a juvenile-onset distal hereditary motor neuropathy caused by heterozygous nonsense mutations in the SPTAN1 gene, which encodes alpha-II spectrin. Penetrance may be variable, and severity differs greatly between patients (Beijer et al., 2019).

checks.claim: HMND11 is a juvenile-onset distal hereditary motor neuropathy.
checks.evidence_quote: Nonsense mutations in alpha-II spectrin in three families with juvenile onset hereditary motor neuropathy.
checks.explanation: The title states juvenile onset, and the abstract refers to distal hereditary motor neuropathies.

checks.claim: HMND11 is caused by heterozygous nonsense mutations in the SPTAN1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified patients with heterozygous nonsense mutations in the αII-spectrin gene, SPTAN1, in three separate dominant hereditary motor neuropathy families

checks.claim: The SPTAN1 gene encodes alpha-II spectrin.
checks.evidence_quote: the αII-spectrin gene, SPTAN1

checks.claim: Penetrance of HMND11 may be variable.
checks.evidence_quote: Variable penetrance was noted for these mutations in two of three families

checks.claim: The severity of HMND11 differs greatly between patients.
checks.evidence_quote: phenotype severity differs greatly between patients

paragraphs.text: Beijer et al. (2019) reported 3 families with juvenile-onset distal hereditary motor neuropathy. Penetrance was variable in 2 of the 3 families, and the severity of the phenotype differed greatly between patients.

paragraphs.text: Beijer et al. (2019) used next-generation sequencing to study affected members of 3 unrelated families with juvenile-onset autosomal dominant distal hereditary motor neuropathy. They found heterozygous nonsense mutations in the SPTAN1 gene. In patient cells, mutant SPTAN1 mRNA was broken down by nonsense-mediated decay, and alpha-II spectrin protein levels were reduced.

paragraphs.text: In patient cells, Beijer et al. (2019) found that mutant SPTAN1 mRNA carrying the nonsense mutations was broken down by nonsense-mediated decay and that alpha-II spectrin protein levels were reduced. They contrasted this with the dominant-negative SPTAN1 mutations previously described as causing a spectrum of epilepsy phenotypes.

checks.explanation: The abstract mentions the earlier dominant-negative epilepsy mutations. It does not explicitly frame them as a contrast to the new mutations; the contrast is only implied.
